title: Sparse-projection KV compaction prototype + fidelity gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: reduce per-GPU KV cache memory by combining sparse projection + blockwise low-bit compaction while preserving downstream generation fidelity. Motivation: continuous batching and long-context workloads (8k+ tokens) are driving KV working set beyond available device memory for certain Dedicated tiers. Prior probes looked at blockwise quant and hybrid fallbacks; this spike builds a prototype that uses an inexpensive sparse projection to reduce activation dimensionality before applying int8/int4 block compaction, with error-compensation sketches kept in small FP8 correction buffers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runs end-to-end on a 32GB A10G instance and reduces KV memory footprint by >=30% for long-context (8k) runs compared to baseline FP16 cache
Token-generation latency increase <= 8% at P50 for steady-state continuous-batching workloads compared to the quantization-disabled baseline
Avg perplexity shift on evaluation suite <= +3% for FP8+projection and <= +6% for INT4+projection with compensation
Automated fallback route implemented: per-request fidelity gate that switches to FP16 cache if projected residual error exceeds threshold
Experiment artifacts (notebooks, perf traces, PR) are linked in ticket and reviewed by runtime team
experiment_plan: 1) Implement sparse projection layer (train-free, randomized sparse matrices + per-block norm scaling) inserted between attention key/query cache writes and storage. 2) Add blockwise quantization pipeline supporting FP8/int8/int4 and a small FP8 residual buffer per block. 3) Implement a lightweight online error estimator (dot-probe) that computes residual magnitude for recently used KV blocks to drive fidelity gates. 4) Run batched synthetic workloads (continuous-batching harness) + representative real prompts (P3 subset + chatty-dialogues) across model sizes: 7B, 13B, 70B. 5) Collect memory, latency, and quality metrics; compare to baseline FP16 and prior INT8-only runs. 6) Iterate on projection sparsity and block sizes to find Pareto frontier. 7) Add graceful fallback: request-level routing to FP16 variant when the estimator triggers. 8) Prepare rollout playbook for Dedicated with knobbed config and safety thresholds.
datasets: Evaluation uses: (a) a 20k-sample held-out mix including Summarization (CNN/DailyMail subset), Dialog (MultiWOZ-like samples), and Code generation prompts; (b) internal long-context chat traces anonymized from dev telemetry (1k sessions); (c) standard perplexity collection from P3-sharded validation slices.
metrics: Primary: KV memory reduction (%), delta perplexity (%), delta logprob (avg), generation latency P50/P95, throughput (tokens/s) under continuous-batching, error estimator false-positive/false-negative rates. Secondary: CPU overhead for projection, GPU kernel occupancy, extra GPU memory for residual buffers.
results_summary: Initial prototype (sparsity 0.15, block size 128, INT8 compaction with FP8 residual) on 13B model: KV footprint reduced ~34%, P50 latency +6% under continuous-batching, perplexity delta +2.6% on eval suite. INT4 runs show ~52% footprint reduction but perplexity delta +5.9% and increased false-positive triggers for fallback. FP8-only projection gave ~22% footprint reduction with negligible quality shift. Early tests on 70B show similar trends but increased latency sensitivity. Error estimator catches ~92% of high-residual blocks (precision 0.78), enabling fallbacks that keep user-visible regressions rare. GPU occupancy increased slightly due to projection kernels; overall throughput impact manageable with kernel fusion planned.
next_steps: Tune projection sparsity and block size sweep (matrix shapes: 256x128, 512x128) to find knee for 70B model
Prototype kernel fusion of projection + quantize steps to reduce latency overhead
Add per-customer rollout flags and runtime knobs in Dedicated to enable/disable projection
Run 7-day stability soak on Dedicated test pool with Canary routing to measure long-tail degradation patterns
Open PR for runtime changes and a design doc describing fidelity-gate thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 0: behind feature flag for internal Dedicated canary (low-traffic customers). Phase 1: enable for internal dev accounts only with aggressive telemetry. Phase 2: opt-in for select customers with SLA guardrails. Include automatic rollback when user-visible metric drift exceeds configured bounds.
blockers: - Need kernel-level support for fused projection->quantize to keep latency within SLO; currently implemented in Python/CUDA prototype. - Telemetry collection hooks for per-block residuals not yet wired into Console metrics pipeline. - Security review pending (residuals buffer durability and potential info leakage analysis).
